items.title: Over 330,000 displaced across Middle East, UNHCR says

featured_image.name: Israeli bombardment of Lebanon sends 100,000 fleeing to war-torn Syria: UN

items.description:
More than 330,000 people have been forcibly displaced across the Middle East and beyond as intensifying hostilities between the United States, Israel, and Iran send shockwaves through a region already hosting millions of refugees, the UN refugee agency said Thursday.[1][2]

UNHCR reported that an estimated 100,000 people fled Tehran in the first 48 hours after US-Israeli strikes began on February 28, with road police recording between 1,000 and 2,000 vehicles departing the capital daily, heading primarily toward northern provinces. Despite the internal exodus, the agency noted "no major increase in cross-border movements from Iran linked to recent events".[3][2][1]

items.title: US and Venezuela formally restore diplomatic relations

featured_image.name: US and Venezuela talk post-Maduro 'transition' - Le Monde

items.description:
The United States and Venezuela formally agreed on Thursday to re-establish diplomatic and consular relations, the State Department announced, capping a two-month diplomatic thaw that began after U.S. forces captured Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro in a military raid on Caracas.[1][2]

"The United States and Venezuela's interim authorities have agreed to re-establish diplomatic and consular relations," the State Department said in a statement dated March 5. The announcement was also confirmed by Reuters and Bloomberg Government.[3][2][1]

items.title: Zelenskyy says Druzhba pipeline could resume within six weeks

featured_image.name: Sources on whether Druzhba pipeline will restart on February 26 |  RBC-Ukraine

items.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on March 5 that the Russian-damaged Druzhba oil pipeline could resume operations within one to one-and-a-half months, even as he reiterated his personal opposition to repairing infrastructure that carries Russian crude to Europe. "We can provide information that resumption may be possible within these one and a half months… But this does not mean that everything that was destroyed will be repaired," Zelenskyy said during a briefing in Kyiv, according to Interfax-Ukraine.[1]

The announcement comes as the European Union weighs providing Ukraine with financial assistance to fix the pipeline, a move aimed at breaking a political deadlock in which Hungary and Slovakia have blocked a €90 billion EU loan for Kyiv and fresh sanctions on Russia.[2][3]

items.title: Iraq's first lady tells US to 'leave the Kurds alone'

featured_image.name: Leave the Kurds Alone,' Says Iraq's First Lady

items.description:
Iraq's First Lady Shanaz Ibrahim Ahmed issued a pointed rebuke of US efforts to enlist Kurdish fighters in the war against Iran, declaring in a statement posted to social media on Thursday, "Leave the Kurds alone. We are not guns for hire."[1][2]

Ahmed's remarks, among the most forceful by a senior Iraqi figure since the conflict began, come days after CNN reported that the CIA is working to arm Kurdish forces along the Iraq-Iran border with the aim of fomenting an uprising inside Iran. President Donald Trump spoke earlier this week with Mustafa Hijri, the president of the Democratic Party of Iranian Kurdistan, and separately reached out to Kurdish leaders in Iraq to discuss military cooperation, according to CNN and other outlets.[3][4]

items.title: Israel orders unprecedented mass evacuation of Beirut suburbs

featured_image.name: Israel issues evacuation orders to 30 towns in southern ...

items.description:
The Israeli military issued unprecedented evacuation orders Thursday for entire neighborhoods in Beirut's southern suburbs, the first time such blanket warnings have covered the Hezbollah-controlled area known as the Dahiyeh, as Israeli airstrikes across Lebanon intensified for a fourth consecutive day.

"Save your lives and evacuate your homes immediately," Israeli military spokesperson Col. Avichay Adraee wrote on X, directing residents of Burj al-Barajneh and Hadath to move east toward Mount Lebanon, and those in Haret Hreik and Shiyah to head north toward Tripoli. Residents were warned not to move south under any circumstances.[1][2]

items.title: Iran says it's ready for US ground invasion, rejects ceasefire

items.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Thursday that Iran is prepared to confront American forces if the United States launches a ground invasion, warning it would be "a big disaster for them." items.title: Trump backs Kurdish offensive against Iran, says goal is 'to win'

featured_image.name: Trump spoke with Kurdish leaders on Iran at Netanyahu's ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump on Thursday voiced support for Kurdish forces launching an offensive into Iran, telling Reuters in an interview, "I think it's wonderful that they want to do that, I'd be all for it." When asked whether the United States would provide or had offered air cover, Trump said, "I can't tell you that," but added that the objective for the Kurds would be "to win."[1]

The remarks came as The Washington Post reported that Trump had offered "extensive U.S. aircover" and other backing to anti-regime Iranian Kurdish groups during calls with Kurdish minority leaders in Iran and Iraq earlier this week.[2]
